chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever deals justly with the people regarding himself will be pleased with how others judge about him.
ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of being fair to others in one's own rights?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the principle of *al-insaf* (self-justice or fairness to oneself) as the foundation for social harmony, suggesting that when one is just in their own claims, others are inclined to judge them favorably. This reflects the Shia ethical emphasis on internal moral integrity manifesting in external social perception, reinforcing the idea that justice is not merely a legal obligation but a character trait that earns trust and respect from the community.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-24 Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his uncle Muhammad ibn Abil-Qasim quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Mahboob, on the authority of some of the companions that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “
Whoever deals justly with the people will be pleased with how others judge about him.”
